overall_assessment: Anonymization works well at HiOF. All 28 packet courses lose their Emneansvarlig/Emneansvarlige names, whether the name is on the label line or the line below, along with the '(Høst yyyy)' title stamps, 'Gjeldende litteraturliste for <semester>' labels, 'Litteraturlist* sist oppdatert' stamps and 'Sist hentet fra FS' footers. No content was over-removed. The one confirmed leak is a free-text 'Foreleser studieåret …:' line at the end of a reading list: its year and e-mail are removed but the lecturer's name stays. All the pre-pass flags are false alarms: 'removed' is high only because the short 2007 and 2022 plans are short, and 'name_like' and 'admin_date' come from reading-list authors and a Lovdata link.

findings.description: A lecturer's name in a free-text staff line at the end of the Litteratur section stays in course_plan. The source line was 'Foreleser studieåret 2018-2019: [navn] ([e-post])'. The generic regexes removed the academic year and the e-mail but not the name. The rubric requires names of teachers in their role at the institution to be removed. Only 1 of the 28 packet courses has this, but the 'Foreleser' label is outside what .anon_hiof() handles, so older plans with similar lines (Foreleser, Faglærer, Kontaktperson) probably leak the same way.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: .anon_hiof() in R/anonymize.R strips names only after an 'Emneansvarlige?:' line, using (?m)^Emneansvarlige?:\s*\n…. No HiOF or generic rule handles a 'Foreleser …:' label followed by a name, and the name has no e-mail or phone pattern to anchor on once the e-mail is removed.
findings.suggested_fix: In .anon_hiof(), before the generic pass, remove staff label lines and the name lines that follow them, e.g. str_remove_all("(?m)^[ \\t]*(?:Foreleser|Forelesere|Faglærer|Faglærere|Kontaktperson)(?: studieåret)?[^\\n:]{0,20}:[ \\t]*\\n?[^\\n]*") (label, optional year, colon, then the rest of that line or the next line). Then scan all published hiof plans for '^(Foreleser|Faglærer|Kontaktperson)' to measure prevalence, and add this case to tests/testthat/test-anonymize.R.

findings.description: Removing an academic year from running prose leaves an ungrammatical sentence: 'vil i 2007/2008 koste' becomes 'vil i koste'. Removing the year itself is correct under the rubric. The dangling preposition is cosmetic damage and does not change the meaning.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: In .anon_generic(), the academic-year pattern \d{4}/\d{2,4} removes only the year and leaves the preposition in front of it.
findings.suggested_fix: Optional: in the academic-year removal, also take a directly preceding 'i '/'for ' when the year is mid-sentence, e.g. (?:\b(?:i|for)[ \t]+)?\d{4}/\d{2,4}\b. Low priority.
